**Visual analysis:**

- Plant: tomato (compound leaves, serrated leaflets — characteristic tomato morphology)
- Affected part: leaves
- Lesions: numerous small, dark brown to black spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Spot size: very small, roughly pinpoint to 1/8 inch
- Some spots show faint yellow halos around them
- Leaf margins show slight yellowing/browning
- No concentric rings visible
- No fungal sporulation (no gray/white/olive fuzz)
- No large necrotic areas or V-shaped lesions

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Small (1/16–1/4 in.) angular black spots with yellow halos on leaves — matches very well. The spots are distinctly small, black/dark brown, and some have yellow margins.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Circular tan-to-gray lesions with pycnidia (tiny dark dots) in centers — the spots here lack tan/gray centers; they are solid dark throughout.
- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**: Would show bronzing of upper leaf surface and blurred-margin necrotic spots — no bronzing visible here.
- **Early_Blight**: Larger darker brown lesions with concentric rings — spots here are much smaller with no rings.
- **Leaf_Mold**: Would show yellow upper spots with olive velvety underside growth — no velvety mold visible.

The small, solid black/dark-brown spots with yellow halos on tomato leaves, without fungal sporulation or concentric rings, best match Bacterial Speck of Tomato.
